findings.title: Remove the committed editor-backup test file
findings.description: This is an editor backup rather than a runnable `*.test.ts` file, so Vitest and TypeScript do not include it. It duplicates the maintained factory test and retains obsolete one-argument `createContextPipeline` calls that no longer match the required options API. Keeping the backup in source control adds dead, stale code and should be removed.

findings.title: Operational adoption failures still become successful error-stub builds
findings.description: Only `AdoptionError` instances take the new rethrow path. However, the real resolver can throw ordinary errors: malformed `.context-forge.toml` parsing from `readAdoptionState` propagates a plain parser error, and guide reads/parsing in `assertGuideSupportsAdoption` can also fail with ordinary errors. Those failures fall through to the generic catch, producing an “Error generating context” string while the CLI/MCP call still succeeds. Expected adoption boundary failures should be normalized to `AdoptionError` with their cause, and a pipeline-level test should verify that malformed project configuration or an unreadable guide rejects the build.

findings.title: Centralize the adoption write-mode values
findings.description: `AdoptionStateWrites` defines `'persist'` and `'read-only'`, but the resolver comparison and the CLI/MCP call sites repeat the literals directly. Renaming either mode therefore requires changing several files, contrary to the project rule that comparison values have one source of truth. Export a constant map and derive the type from it, then use the constants at every call site.
